candidate_name: Energy City Port Qasim -- floating + land-based LNG terminal
sponsor_or_proposer: Government of Pakistan (Ministry of Maritime Affairs / Port Qasim Authority) -- no private developer identified
current_state: Federal Maritime Affairs Minister Muhammad Junaid Anwar said (Jul 2026) that a 'floating LNG terminal' is part of a broader Port Qasim 'Energy City' plan (alongside a $1.4bn 'Sea 2 Steel' shipbuilding project, oil storage, and container/cargo terminals), and that a technical study for a separate LAND-BASED LNG terminal has been completed, expected to attract $3-4bn investment. 'Multiple locations are currently being considered.'
missing_threshold_elements: No sponsor/developer company named for either the floating or land-based component; no specific site (multiple still 'being considered'); no capacity, cost breakdown, or timeline beyond the aggregate $3-4bn figure -- fails the add-bar (needs sponsor + approx location + concrete step).
watch_for: A named private sponsor/consortium, a specific Port Qasim site, or an OGRA filing tied to this initiative.
notes: Distinct from the existing Energas/Tabeer/GasPort-2/LNG-Easy proposed terminals already in GEM -- this is a separate, vaguer govt-led umbrella initiative. Also distinct from the Gwadar Energy City item below (different port, different sponsor mix).

candidate_name: Gwadar Energy City -- LNG/LPG terminal component
sponsor_or_proposer: Government of Pakistan; Kuwait reportedly expressing interest (per Jun 2026 report) -- no developer named
current_state: A June 2026 report describes a proposed 'Energy City' at Gwadar Port focused primarily on strategic crude-oil storage for oil-producing countries, with the plan also including 'LNG and LPG terminals.' No detail beyond that one sentence.
missing_threshold_elements: No sponsor, no site within Gwadar, no capacity, no cost, no timeline for the LNG/LPG component specifically -- fails the add-bar.
watch_for: A named sponsor or a specific Gwadar site/capacity for the LNG (not just crude-storage) component.
notes: This revives the Gwadar-area LNG conversation last seen with the now-shelved Daewoo Gas LNG Terminal (same general Gwadar Port area, different, unnamed sponsor) -- worth checking whether a future concrete announcement is a genuinely new sponsor or a Daewoo Gas successor/rename.
